component.name: Montech HyperFlow Display
component.summary: Unofficial panel indicator for the Montech HyperFlow Digital AIO pump-head display

description.p: Montech HyperFlow Display drives the 7-segment temperature readout on a Montech HyperFlow Digital AIO pump head from Linux. It is an unofficial, community-written driver: not produced, endorsed, supported, reviewed or approved by Montech, by TCOMAS, or by SEMICO. Do not contact any of them about it. The names are used only to say which hardware it talks to.
Montech's own application is Windows-only. The wire protocol used here was documented from scratch for interoperability. No vendor code, firmware, fonts or artwork is shipped, and none is required.
The hardware is USB 1a2c:4e85, OEM platform TCOMAS DH-C100. Rebrands of the same pump head sold under other names very likely work unchanged.
This package provides the panel indicator, which shows:

ul.li: The temperature the pump head is currently displaying
Celsius or Fahrenheit, switchable from the menu
CPU or GPU as the tracked sensor
Start and stop for the background display service
A one-click blank for the display

description.p: The indicator is a client and never opens the device itself. A background system service owns the pump head, so the display keeps working while you are logged out or sitting at the login screen. The service, its udev rule and its privileged helper are installed by the native montech-hyperflow package, which must be present on the host for this indicator to do anything beyond report that the daemon is missing.

ul.li: Device discovery by HID usage page rather than by node number, so the correct interface is picked when the cooler exposes several
Live CPU temperature tracking, with GPU as an alternative source
Panel indicator with unit, source, service and blank controls
System service runs unprivileged as a transient user
The display is reopened automatically after unplug or resume
